page: Amazon Web Services m8ib.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors running at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz. The hardware platform provides 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs via multithreading, coupled with 768 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced general-purpose ratio of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Operating without hypervisor overhead, this bare-metal configuration grants complete direct access to the underlying hardware resources.

In terms of connectivity and I/O, the instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps, enabling high-throughput inter-node communication and fast network storage access. Notably, the m8ib.metal-48xl includes no bundled local storage, necessitating external network-attached volumes for persistent data operations. The platform also omits discrete hardware accelerators, dedicating all system resources to central CPU compute and large memory tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture eliminates virtualization performance penalties, offering high compute density across its 192 dedicated processing threads. Organizations running large monolithic systems or dense container clusters benefit from the consolidated memory footprint and high network throughput. Recommended workloads include large-scale web application serving, memory-resident caching clusters, enterprise resource planning systems, high-concurrency backend services, and distributed compute nodes reliant on remote block storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m8ib.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server designed for high-density enterprise workloads. Powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors clocked at 3.9 GHz, it features 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs alongside 768 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The bare-metal architecture removes hypervisor virtualization layers, giving workloads full direct access to raw processor capabilities. Network connectivity is substantial, offering a baseline throughput of 200 Gbps for distributed environments and external storage communication. A key architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of bundled local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistence, as well as the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. The m8ib.metal-48xl provides an efficient consolidated footprint for enterprise backend infrastructure, large-scale web serving fleets, monolithic application hosts, high-concurrency microservices, and container orchestration platforms.
